q: What does this sign mean?
a: Narrow bridge ahead
e: Two lines bending in on both sides = narrow bridge.
s: Narrow bridge ahead.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: A road branches off ahead
w: Road forks to the right: you must turn
e: A side road branching off to one side. A full cross (+) would be an intersection.
s: Road branching off ahead.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Roundabout ahead: reduce speed
e: The arrows show traffic moves counter-clockwise inside the roundabout.
s: Roundabout Ahead. Reduce Speed.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Drivers on the side road ahead don't have a clear view of traffic
e: Hidden side road: be ready for drivers pulling out who can't see you well.
s: Drivers on the sideroad at the intersection ahead don't have a clear view of traffic.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: The bridge ahead lifts or swings to let boats pass
e: A bridge with water underneath and a raised section = lift or swing bridge.
s: The bridge ahead lifts or swings to let boats pass.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: The paved surface ends ahead
e: The road picture changes from paved to dotted gravel: pavement ends.
s: Paved surface ends ahead.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Bicycle crossing ahead
e: Yellow diamond with a bike = bikes cross ahead. A green circle bike sign is a bike route.
s: Bicycle crossing ahead.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Pavement is slippery when wet; slow down and drive with caution
e: A car with wavy skid marks = slippery when wet.
s: Pavement is slippery when wet. Slow down and drive with caution.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Steep hill ahead; you may need a lower gear
e: A truck on a slope with a percent grade = steep hill.
s: Steep hill ahead. You may need to use a lower gear.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Snowmobiles cross this road
e: A yellow diamond warns that snowmobiles cross here.
s: Snowmobiles cross this road.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Underpass ahead; the number shows how much height clearance you have
e: Arrows pointing up and down with a height = low underpass. Take care in a tall vehicle.
s: Underpass ahead. Take care if you are driving a tall vehicle. Sign shows how much room you have.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Bump or uneven pavement ahead
e: Slow down and keep control of your vehicle.
s: Bump or uneven pavement on the road ahead.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Deer regularly cross this road
w: No animals allowed on the road
e: Be alert for animals, especially from dusk to dawn.
s: Deer regularly cross this road; be alert for animals.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Watch for fallen rock
e: Be prepared to avoid rocks on the road.
s: Watch for fallen rock and be prepared to avoid a collision.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: There may be water flowing over the road
e: Water across the road picture = flooding possible.
s: There may be water flowing over the road.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Watch for pedestrians and be prepared to share the road with them
e: A yellow diamond with a walking person = pedestrians may be on or near the road.
s: Watch for pedestrians and be prepared to share the road with them.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Truck entrance on the right side of the road ahead
w: Trucks must use the right lane
e: If the truck is drawn on the left, the entrance is on the left.
s: Truck entrance on the right side of the road ahead.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Intersection ahead; the wide arrow shows which road has the right-of-way
e: The thicker arrow shows which direction of traffic has the right-of-way.
s: Intersection ahead. The arrow shows which direction of traffic has the right-of-way.

q: Which sign warns of a stop sign ahead?
a: signs/3-1-50a.jpg
e: A yellow diamond with a small red octagon and an arrow = stop sign ahead. Slow down.
s: Stop sign ahead. Slow down.

q: Which sign warns of traffic lights ahead?
a: signs/3-1-56a.jpg
e: A yellow diamond showing a traffic light.
s: Traffic lights ahead. Slow down.

q: Which sign means a winding road ahead?
a: signs/3-1-46a.jpg
e: The arrow wiggles back and forth more than once = winding road.
s: Winding road ahead.

q: Which sign is posted in groups to guide drivers around a sharp curve?
a: signs/3-1-45a.jpg
e: Chevron (arrowhead) signs come in groups around sharp curves.
s: Chevron (arrowhead) signs are posted in groups to guide drivers around sharp curves in the road.

q: Which sign marks a hazard close to the edge of the road?
a: signs/3-1-53a.jpg
e: The hazard marker has diagonal stripes; the lines slope down toward the side where you may safely pass.
s: Hazard close to the edge of the road.

q: Which sign means: divided highway begins?
a: signs/3-1-54a.jpg
e: The arrows split around a median: the road divides ahead. Keep to the right-hand road.
s: Divided highway begins: traffic travels in both directions on separated roads ahead.

q: Which sign means: divided highway ends?
a: signs/3-1-60a.jpg
e: The median ends and both directions share the same road ahead.
s: Divided highway ends: traffic travels in both directions on the same road ahead.

q: Which sign means the right lane ends ahead?
a: signs/3-1-55a.jpg
e: One lane line bends in on the right = right lane ends. Merge safely to the left.
s: Right lane ends ahead.

q: Which sign means two roads going the same direction are about to join into one?
a: signs/3-1-58a.jpg
e: Merge sign: drivers on both roads share the job of merging safely.
s: Two roads going in the same direction are about to join into one.

q: Which sign warns of a railway crossing ahead and shows the angle of the tracks?
a: signs/3-1-63a.jpg
e: The yellow diamond with tracks crossing the road warns before the crossing.
s: Railway crossing ahead. Be alert for trains. This sign also shows the angle at which the railway tracks cross the road.

q: Which sign tells drivers to provide safe space on the road for cyclists?
e: The "share the road" sign shows a car and a cyclist side by side.
s: The share the road sign is used to warn motorists that they are to provide safe space on the road for cyclists and other vehicles.

q: Which sign means: share the road with oncoming traffic (two-way traffic)?
a: signs/3-1-51a.jpg
e: Two arrows pointing opposite ways in a yellow diamond = two-way traffic.
s: Share the road with oncoming traffic.

q: Which sign warns of a hidden school bus stop ahead?
a: signs/3-1-71a2.jpg
e: A yellow diamond with a school bus and children.
s: This sign warns you that you are coming to a hidden school bus stop.

q: Which sign warns of an upcoming bus entrance on the right?
a: signs/3-1-71a.jpg
e: Look at the vehicle: a bus (not a truck or fire truck). Be ready to yield to buses entering.
s: Indicates an upcoming bus entrance on the right and vehicles should be prepared to yield to buses entering the roadway.

q: Which sign warns of an upcoming fire truck entrance?
a: signs/3-1-71b2.jpg
e: A yellow diamond with a fire truck. Be ready to yield to fire trucks entering the road.
s: Indicates an upcoming fire truck entrance on the right and vehicles should be prepared to yield to fire trucks entering the roadway.

q: Which sign warns of a school crossing?
a: signs/3-1-72.jpg
e: School crossing signs are fluorescent yellow/green rectangles with children crossing.
s: These signs warn of a school crossing.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Slight bend or curve in the road ahead
e: A gently curved arrow = slight bend. A right-angle arrow = sharp turn.
s: Slight bend or curve in the road ahead.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Sharp bend or turn in the road ahead
e: The arrow bends at a right angle = sharp turn.
s: Sharp bend or turn in the road ahead.

q: What does this sign with a checkerboard border mean?
a: Sharp turn in the direction of the arrow: danger, slow down
w: Keep right of the traffic island
e: The checkerboard border warns of danger.
s: Sharp turn or bend in the road in the direction of the arrow.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Pavement narrows ahead
e: Both edges come in a little = the pavement narrows. A narrow bridge sign has bracket-shaped lines.
s: Pavement narrows ahead.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Divided highway ends: two-way traffic on the same road ahead
w: Merge with traffic from the left
Keep right of the traffic island
e: The divider stops and the arrows come together: the divided highway ends. Keep to the right.
s: Divided highway ends: traffic travels in both directions on the same road ahead. Keep to the right-hand road.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Divided highway begins: keep to the right-hand road
e: The arrows separate around a divider: two separate one-way roads ahead.
s: Divided highway begins: traffic travels in both directions on separated roads ahead. Keep to the right-hand road. Each road carries one-way traffic.

q: Two roads join into one at this sign. Who is responsible for merging safely?
a: Drivers on both roads, equally
w: Only drivers on the road that ends
Only drivers on the main road
e: At a merge, drivers on both roads share the job of merging smoothly and safely.
s: Drivers on both roads are equally responsible for seeing that traffic merges smoothly and safely.

q: This square yellow sign is posted under a curve warning. What does the number mean?
a: The maximum safe speed for the curve
w: The regular speed limit for the road
The minimum speed for the curve
The distance to the curve in metres
e: The yellow advisory sign under a curve sign shows the safe speed for that curve.
s: Posted under a curve warning, this sign shows the maximum safe speed for the curve.

q: This square yellow sign is posted at a freeway ramp. What does it show?
a: The maximum safe speed on the ramp
w: The speed limit on the freeway
e: Yellow advisory speed = safe speed for the ramp. Speed limit signs are white.
s: Shows maximum safe speed on ramp.

q: Which vehicle is shown, and what does the sign warn?
a: A truck: truck entrance on the right side ahead
w: A bus: bus entrance on the right
A fire truck: fire hall entrance
A tractor: farm vehicles on the road
e: Truck = truck entrance. The bus and fire truck entrance signs look similar. Check the vehicle.
s: Truck entrance on the right side of the road ahead.

q: What does this yellow diamond sign warn of?
a: A hidden school bus stop ahead
w: A school zone with a lower speed limit
A bus entrance on the right
e: Slow down, watch for children and for a school bus with flashing red lights.
s: This sign warns you that you are coming to a hidden school bus stop.

q: This sign shows a car and a bicycle side by side. What does it mean?
a: Share the road: give cyclists and other vehicles safe space
e: Share the road = give cyclists room, and both take extra care on this stretch.
s: The share the road sign is used to warn motorists that they are to provide safe space on the road for cyclists and other vehicles.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Share the road with oncoming traffic (two-way traffic)
e: Arrows going opposite ways = traffic comes toward you in the other lane.
s: Share the road with oncoming traffic.

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Railway crossing ahead; the sign shows the angle of the tracks
e: The yellow diamond warns of the crossing. The red-and-white X sign is at the crossing itself.
s: Railway crossing ahead. Be alert for trains.

q: This sign has black and yellow diagonal stripes. What does it mean?
a: Hazard close to the edge of the road; pass on the side the lines slope down to
e: The hazard marker shows an object near the road, and which side to pass on.
s: The downward lines show the side on which you may safely pass.

q: What is this sign, and where do you see it?
a: A chevron, posted in groups to guide you around a sharp curve
w: A hazard marker on a bridge pier
A detour arrow in construction zones
e: Chevrons = arrowheads guiding you around a sharp curve.
s: Chevron (arrowhead) signs are posted in groups to guide drivers around sharp curves in the road.

q: What kind of sign is this?
a: Warning
e: Yellow diamond = warning of a dangerous or unusual condition.
s: They are usually diamond-shaped and have a yellow background with black letters or symbols.

q: What kind of sign is this?
a: Warning
e: Yellow diamond = warning. Here: deer crossing.
s: These signs warn of dangerous or unusual conditions ahead

q: What kind of sign is this?
a: Warning
e: It's yellow, so it's a permanent warning (steep hill). Orange would mean a temporary condition.
s: They are usually diamond-shaped and have a yellow background with black letters or symbols.

q: What colour is this school crossing sign?
a: Fluorescent yellow/green
e: School signs use fluorescent yellow/green so they stand out.
s: These signs warn of a school crossing.

q: What does the black-and-white checkered edge on this sign add?
a: It warns of danger: slow down and be careful
w: It means the road is closed
It shows the end of a construction zone
e: A checkerboard border means danger.
s: The checkerboard border warns of danger.

q: Why is this bicycle sign a yellow diamond instead of a green circle?
a: It's a warning (bicycles cross ahead), not a regulatory sign
w: It means bicycles are not allowed
It marks an official bike route
It's a temporary sign for road work
e: Yellow diamond = warning. A green circle would be a regulatory "allowed" sign.
s: Bicycle crossing ahead.

q: This is a square yellow sign with a speed on it. What kind of sign is it?
a: Warning (advisory safe speed)
e: It's yellow, so it's a warning showing the safe speed for a curve or ramp, not the speed limit.
s: Posted under a curve warning, this sign shows the maximum safe speed for the curve.

q: What kind of sign is this?
a: Warning
e: Yellow diamond = warning. Here: traffic lights ahead.
s: Traffic lights ahead. Slow down.

q: You're in the right lane and see this sign. What must you do?
a: Merge safely with traffic in the lane to your left
w: Speed up and pass the cars on your left
Stop at the end of the lane
e: Right lane ends: signal, check your blind spot and merge left.
s: If you are in the right-hand lane, you must merge safely with traffic in the lane to the left.

q: How do you use this sign to pass the hazard?
a: Pass on the side the stripes slope down toward
w: Pass on the side the stripes slope up toward
Stop and wait for a flag person
e: The downward lines show the safe side to pass on.
s: The downward lines show the side on which you may safely pass.

q: What may you need to do when you see this sign?
a: Use a lower gear
w: Speed up to climb the hill
Stop at the top of the hill
e: Steep hill: a lower gear helps control your speed.
s: You may need to use a lower gear.

q: What should you be prepared to do when you see this sign?
a: Yield to fire trucks entering the roadway
w: Stop until a fire truck comes out
Speed up to clear the entrance
e: Fire truck entrance: be ready to yield.
s: vehicles should be prepared to yield to fire trucks entering the roadway

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
a: Slow down and watch for children and a school bus with flashing red lights
w: Keep your speed; it only applies to buses
e: Hidden school bus stop: slow down and drive with extra caution.
s: Slow down, drive with extra caution, watch for children and for a school bus with flashing red lights.

q: You see this sign. What should you do?
a: Keep to the right: traffic ahead travels both ways on the same road
w: Speed up before the road narrows
e: Divided highway ends: oncoming traffic will be on the same road, so keep right.
s: Divided highway ends: traffic travels in both directions on the same road ahead. Keep to the right-hand road.

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
a: Watch for children and follow the directions of the crossing guard or school safety patroller
w: Speed up to clear the crossing
Stop only if you see a school bus
e: School crossing: watch for children and obey the crossing guard.
s: Watch for children and follow the directions of the crossing guard or school safety patroller.

q: What should you do when you see this sign?
a: Slow down and get ready to stop at the stop sign ahead
w: Speed up before the light changes
Yield only to traffic on your right
e: Stop sign ahead: slow down.
s: Stop sign ahead. Slow down.

q: Who most needs to pay attention to this sign?
a: Drivers of tall vehicles: the number shows the height clearance
w: Drivers of wide vehicles: it's the road width
Drivers towing trailers longer than 3.9 m
e: Low underpass: take care if you're driving a tall vehicle.
s: Take care if you are driving a tall vehicle.

q: You see this sign. What should you expect?
a: Drivers coming from the side road may not see you, so be ready
w: You must stop at the side road
Only trucks use the side road
e: Hidden side road: drivers there don't have a clear view of traffic.
s: Drivers on the sideroad at the intersection ahead don't have a clear view of traffic.
